description: Conformance corpus for code generation reached through a constructor chain. Every value a script can touch (a literal function, a built-in, a binding, a value a binding returned, an error a binding threw, an argument a callback received) leads by `.constructor` to some realm's `Function`. That `Function` must refuse to compile a string, in every runtime, whatever realm it belongs to.
notes: Each case's `expr` is spliced into `template` at `EXPR`, and the script must evaluate to `"blocked"`: the constructor it reached threw a `TypeError`. `reached:...` means a string compiled (an eval hole, and a host escape if the reached `Function` belongs to the host realm). `threw:...` means something other than a `TypeError` stopped it, which is a conformance failure even though nothing escaped.

`probe.data` returns `{ "list": [1, { "k": "v" }] }`. `probe.fail` throws a host error. `probe.call(path, callArgs, ...payload)` is the callback probe from `callback-tests.json`: it calls the callback at `path` with `callArgs`.

A runtime whose sandbox is a separate engine (QuickJS, Jint) reaches only its own engine's `Function`, so a hole there is an eval violation rather than a host escape. A runtime that shares the host's engine (Node's `vm`) reaches the host's `Function` from any host-realm value, which is a full escape; that is why values crossing into a `vm` context must be re-created in the context's realm.
template: (function () { try { var make = EXPR; if (typeof make === 'string') return 'reached:' + make; var made = make('return typeof process'); if (typeof made === 'function') made = made(); return 'reached:' + String(made); } catch (e) { return e && e.name === 'TypeError' ? 'blocked' : 'threw:' + (e && e.name); } })()

call.description: Calls the callback at path with callArgs.

cases.name: a nested object a binding returned
